name: IoWriteQueue_FlushPending
behavior: When the queue is nonempty, copies the fixed transfer-command executor to temporary RAM, invokes it with the queue and count, then clears the count.

probe.hypothesis: An ordinary-C DMA descriptor representation can publish the source, destination, and control words with the reference standalone three-register transfer.
probe.acceptance: Canonical complete video-DMA queue composition is byte-exact and all eleven existing exact owners remain byte-exact.
tested: direct scalar, compound-aggregate, volatile, nonvolatile, and post-increment DMA register stores
local, VLA-backed, and by-value three-word descriptors
count, zero, declaration-lifetime, and padding variants
probe.result: No canonical form emits the reference standalone three-register store followed by base restoration. Scalar and post-increment forms use scalar or one-register stores; aggregate forms use a twelve-byte staging copy with LDMIA/STMIA and grow to 108 or 112 bytes. Removing the existing padding probe regresses to 92 bytes and 44 differing halfwords.

remaining: The current VLA and call behavior are credible, but the reference needs a standalone DMA publication with the count, zero, and control-base lifetimes allocated differently. The approved compiler's volatile multiple-transfer and BLKmode paths explain the tested alternatives, but do not prove that no ordinary-C source can emit the owner. Retain structured assembly; no permanent compiler classification is claimed.
notes: All measurements compile the complete declared video-dma-queue reconstruction composition once with canonical GCC 2.96.
No inline assembly, fixed-register variable, compiler barrier, forbidden ABI, copied instruction bytes, compiler modification, or per-owner flag override was used.
This candidate claims zero DONE bytes.
